aims: Assess whether apparent butterfly–host identity effect is dependent on one of the six butterfly families
Assess Monte Carlo chain stability to an independent seed
statistic: Far cross-Level1 climate-analogue minus climate-discordant gain in regional potential butterfly resource Jaccard, recalculated excluding one complete butterfly family.
null: Same butterfly-family×botanical-family-constrained host link swaps that preserve plant geography, butterfly host counts within plant families, and plant users within butterfly families. Recalculate the family-excluded statistic on each null draw with identical pairs and masks.

assessment.negative_excess_on_any_removal: describe non-general concentration rather than claim a general effect
assessment.p_values: exploratory sensitivity, not independent confirmatory tests
assessment.source_drift: observed all-family score must equal 0.09843700070646613 and source family panel=6

boundaries: The null does not preserve each butterfly's realized larval niche or overall added-region number
The response is derived from plant maps and known HOSTS links, not realized local larval use
